output:
Here's the post, at about 378 words and roughly 2,300 characters with spaces:

The Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms wrapped up on Saturday, and on behalf of the organising team (Ketaki Joglekar, Faizan Mirza and myself) I want to put our thanks on record.

Some numbers first. We received 112 applications and selected 41 participants, MSc and early PhD students from 9 states, on the basis of a statement and one reference. The school ran from 5 to 7 November in Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune. The institute's student initiative grant of Rs 2.4 lakh covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students.

Thank you to our three speakers. Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari came from Hyderabad to lecture on Mordell-Weil, Dr. Sunanda Iyer came from Chennai to lecture on modular forms, and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki joined online from Kraków for computations in Sage.

Thank you to Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, our faculty mentor, for her guidance throughout. Mr. Prakash Salunke from the department office sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm when our booking got messed up, and I don't know what we would have done without him. Six PhD students volunteered as TAs and ran the problem sessions. That format worked well and we intend to keep it.

Two moments I will remember. On the second afternoon the power went for nearly two hours and the laptops died. We moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards, and it turned out to be the best session of the three days. And an MSc student from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Sunanda ma'am's notes. She corrected it live and thanked him.

For MSc students I think small schools like this matter more than big conferences. At a big conference you mostly listen. In a room of 41 you get to actually ask questions.

To the participants: thank you for coming, and for staying with the problems even after the lights went out.

The slides and problem sheets will be up on the department website within two weeks, for participants and for anyone else who wants to work through them.

We hope to run a second edition in late 2027. That depends on the grant coming through, so I can't promise yet, but we will certainly try.

I kept "Sunanda ma'am" as you wrote it. If you'd prefer something more formal for the wider audience, change it to "Dr. Iyer's notes".
